newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Luxembourg PM sees success at Amsterdam EU summit.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg PM sees success at Amsterdam EU summit.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker, who brokered an original deal between France and Germany on the stability pact in December, said on Sunday he believed there would be success at the EU summit in Amsterdam.
Asked on arrival whether he had been negotiating with Paris and Bonn on the new dispute over the issue, he told reporters: "I had sufficient contact in order to know that we will have success."

Juncker was among the first EU leaders arriving for the June 16-17 summit, which has been overshadowed by a Franco-German rift over the new French government's insistence on putting more emphasis on jobs in the drive towards European monetary union (EMU). EU finance ministers were to meet on the issue later on Sunday.
The disagreement between Bonn and Paris, which normally form a strong alliance at the centre of EU integration, was prompted by this month's socialist victory in French parliamentary elections.
The split threatens to dominate the two-day meeting which was supposed to culminate in agreement on a new treaty setting Europe's course for the next century.
But new French premier Lionel Jospin has told his partners he wants greater emphasis given to creating jobs in the 15-member bloc. He is hostile to the economic austerity required to qualify for EMU.
